report.incident_summary: Conveyor 2 stopped at 14:20:22 on 2026-01-15 after a sequence of alarms: low cooling flow at 14:14, motor temperature exceeding 65 °C at 14:18, and a thermal shutdown at 14:20 when motor temperature reached 75 °C. The motor current and conveyor speed dropped to zero and the controller entered STOPPED state.
report.leading_hypothesis: Insufficient cooling flow caused motor overheating, leading the controller to execute a thermal shutdown.

timeline.observation: Cooling flow alarm (flow 0.45 L/min) triggered; motor running at normal speed.
Motor temperature alarm (65.08 °C) triggered while cooling flow remained low (0.56 L/min).
Thermal shutdown executed; motor temperature 75.02 °C, motor current 0 A, conveyor speed 0 m/s, controller STOPPED.

supporting_evidence.finding: Cooling flow dropped to 0.45 L/min, below the 2 L/min threshold defined in the manual.
Motor temperature reached 65.08 °C, exceeding the 65 °C limit for MOTOR_TEMP_HIGH.
Controller issued THERMAL_SHUTDOWN at 75.02 °C, stopping the conveyor.
Triggered when cooling flow falls below 2 L/min.
Controller stops conveyor when motor temperature reaches 75 °C; expected zero speed and current.
On 2026-01-06, cooling filter was cleaned and flow restored to normal.
On 2026-01-13, temperature sensor calibration confirmed readings within tolerance.

alternative_explanations: Faulty temperature sensor could have reported an artificially high temperature.
Mechanical jam or bearing failure could have increased motor load, raising temperature.
Communication outage between sensor and controller might have caused erroneous shutdown.
missing_evidence: Independent verification of cooling flow (e.g., secondary flow meter).
Physical inspection of cooling pump, pipes, and valves for blockage or failure.
Cross‑check of motor temperature with an external temperature probe.
Controller log details surrounding the THERMAL_SHUTDOWN command.
recommended_checks: Inspect cooling pump operation and verify pump pressure.
Examine cooling pipe and valve positions for obstructions or leaks.
Validate flow sensor accuracy with a calibrated reference flow meter.
Perform an independent temperature measurement on the motor housing.
Review controller firmware logs for any communication errors preceding shutdown.
Confirm that the cooling filter remains clean and that no debris has re‑accumulated.

note: Structured evidence checks passed. Narrative and causal claims are not fully verified.
